Diego: hi team, Diego here. first day trying to run the runtime in a rootless podman container. build succeeded but the runtime process fails at startup: dlopen failed: libnvidia-ml.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory. python traceback shows OSError when importing nvml: 'nvmlDeviceGetCount' unresolved. any quick pointers?

Leah: welcome! rootless containers + NVIDIA can be flaky. two likely causes: (A) driver libs not mounted into the user namespace, or (B) /run/nvidia udev/socket not visible so NVML can't talk to the driver. which runtime are you using (docker, podman, containerd)? and are you using nvidia-container-toolkit or the nvidia-container-plugin for containerd?

Diego: using podman rootless (Fedora laptop). I tried bind-mounting /usr/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1 into /usr/lib64 in the container but NVML still errors with permission denied on /run/nvidia/uvm. podman run command: 
```bash
podman run --rm -it \
  -v /usr/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1:/usr/lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1:ro \
  my-runtime:dev bash
```

Kasper: binding libs alone often isn't enough for NVML. NVML expects device nodes and driver-managed sockets under /run/nvidia and certain cgroup /dev access. Rootless podman isolates cgroups and may not allow nvidia-container-cli to mount host driver files. For podman we usually either run privileged rootful containers for GPU or use docker with nvidia-container-toolkit. If you must use rootless, ensure user namespaces remap and that `--device /dev/nvidia0` (and nvidiactl, nvidia-uvm) can be passed and that /run/nvidia is bind-mounted. Podman has `--devices` and `--security-opt=label=disable` flags that help.

Diego: tried `--device /dev/nvidia0 --device /dev/nvidiactl --device /dev/nvidia-uvm` and `-v /run/nvidia:/run/nvidia:ro` but still see NVML init fail with "NVML: Insufficient Permissions". Host nvidia-smi works as my user (I added myself to video group). Not sure what's blocked in the container.

Leah: rootless userns can change uid/gid of mounted files, so the video group ownership inside container might not match. Quick tests: `ls -l /run/nvidia` on host (note owner/group) and inside container (after mount) to see mapped UIDs. If UIDs don't map, NVML won't open the device nodes. Two workarounds: 1) run podman in rootful mode for GPU workflows; 2) use `podman --userns=keep-id` and mount /run/nvidia and devices, or 3) use `nvidia-container-toolkit` with docker which handles mapping automatically.

Diego: `ls -l` host: `crw-rw----+ 1 root video 195, 0 Jun  1 10:00 /dev/nvidia0`. inside rootless container the device shows as `crw-rw---- 1 100000 100000 195, 0`. so user mapping changed. keep-id sounds promising. anyone used keep-id for podman + nvidia successfully?

Kasper: we used `--userns=keep-id` plus `--device` and `--group-add video` on Fedora. Example we share internally: 
```bash
podman run -it --rm \
  --userns=keep-id \
  --device /dev/nvidia0 --device /dev/nvidiactl --device /dev/nvidia-uvm \
  -v /run/nvidia:/run/nvidia:ro \
  --group-add video \
  my-runtime:dev bash
```
Also ensure `sysctl kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1` is set if your distro denies user namespaces. If keep-id still fails, fallback to rootful.

Diego: tried keep-id + group-add video and now python NVML import works and runtime proceeds past the nvml init. thank you!

Leah: awesome. for CI note: our CI uses docker + nvidia-container-toolkit, but we have a small preflight for developers using podman. snippet we keep in docs: 
```bash
# quick check inside runtime image
python - <<'PY'
import ctypes
try:
  ctypes.CDLL('libnvidia-ml.so.1')
  print('ok')
except Exception as e:
  print('missing nvml:', e)
  exit(1)
PY

# check devices
ls -l /dev/nvidia*
ls -l /run/nvidia
```
And we add a note to onboarding: prefer docker for day-0 GPU dev on Linux, or use podman with --userns=keep-id and group-add video.

ops-bot: CI: added podman GPU troubleshooting link to the eng-runtime onboarding checklist.

Diego: super helpful, thanks everyone. i'll update my devcontainer and the PR with a note about podman keep-id. excited to be here :rocket:
